item.title: 软阴影别用同一组采样偏移：从白噪声到时空蓝噪声，抖动算法该怎么选 ｜ 阴影采样抖动算法全解析：从白噪声到时空蓝噪声
item.category: 公众号·游戏AI编程与图形渲染
item.description:
一句话：采样核形状与抖动是两个正交问题；抖动把低频条纹换成可被 TAA 抹掉的高频噪声。

要点：

  • PCSS 这类只能用 16–32 次采样逼近连续积分，所有像素共用同一组偏移会得到肉眼可见的条带（banding），因为相邻像素遮挡值完全相同
  • 正解是给每个像素不同抖动，把空间规则条纹打散成高频噪声——人眼更能容忍，且能被 TAA/时域累积/降噪器抹掉，而条纹不能
  • 先分清两个正交概念：采样核形状（所有像素共用的 tap 分布，均匀网格最差、泊松盘最好）与抖动（每像素偏移的时序/空间分布，白噪声→蓝噪声→时空蓝噪声）

为什么值得看：阴影抖动是所有实时软阴影实现都绕不开的一层，但多数团队只是随手叠个 hash。这篇把「核形状」与「抖动」分开讲并给出对比表与选型建议，属于可以直接拿去改 shader 的那类内容。

中文摘要：做软阴影（PCF/PCSS）或者任何有限次采样的效果，都会遇到采样点不够的问题：PCSS 里只能用 16–32 次采样逼近连续积分，若所有像素共用同一组采样偏移，得到的不是噪声而是肉眼可见的条带——同一光源下相邻像素算出的遮挡值完全相同。文章给出的统一解法是给每个像素施加不同抖动，把空间上规则的条带打散成高频噪声：噪声虽然难看，但高频部分人眼更能容忍，而且能被 TAA、时域累积或降噪器抹掉，条带则不能。全文先把两个容易混淆的概念分开——采样核的形状（所有像素共用的 tap 摆放，均匀网格最差、泊松盘最好）与抖动（每像素偏移的分布，白噪声到时空蓝噪声），再逐一给出原理、公式与可直接抄的代码，最后给对比表与实战选型建议。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：公众号·游戏AI编程与图形渲染（中文）

原文发布：2026-10-15

本期推送：2026-10-28

做软阴影（PCF / PCSS）或者任何有限次采样的效果时，都会遇到同一个问题：采样点不够用。

比如 PCSS 里你只能用 16~32 次采样去逼近一个连续积分，如果所有像素都用同一组采样偏移，结果不是噪声，而是一条一条肉眼可见的带状条纹（banding）——因为同一个光源下相邻像素算出来的遮挡值完全相同。

解决思路非常统一：给每个像素施加一个不同的抖动（dither），把空间上规则的 banding 打散成高频噪声。噪声虽然难看，但它有两个好处：

  • 高频噪声对人眼远比低频条纹「友好」；
  • 噪声可以被 TAA / 时域累积 / 降噪器轻松抹掉，而条纹不能。

    • 下面这张图就是全文的直觉起点——同一条连续的半影梯度，欠采样后变成刺眼的条纹，而抖动把条纹换成了人眼更能容忍、且可被时域滤波抹掉的噪声：

    这篇文章把阴影采样里常用的抖动算法系统梳理一遍，给出原理、公式和可直接抄的代码，最后给一张对比表和实战选型建议。

    先用一张流程图把整条采样链路串起来，后面每一节都对应图里的一个方块：

    一、先分清两个正交的概念

    很多人会把「泊松盘采样」和「蓝噪声抖动」混为一谈，其实它们作用在完全不同的环节。一个带抖动的阴影采样器，由两部分组成：

    ① 采样核的形状（所有像素共用）：n 个 tap 在圆盘/平面上怎么摆。

  • 均匀网格：最差，方向性明显；
  • 均匀圆盘（极坐标均匀）：一般；
  • 泊松盘（Poisson Disk）：任意两点距离有下限，覆盖均匀无聚集，是软阴影采样核的事实标准。

    • ② 逐像素的去相关源（每像素不同）：怎么让相邻像素用「同一核的不同旋转/不同排列」。

  • 哈希白噪声、Wang Hash；
  • IGN（Interleaved Gradient Noise）；
  • Bayer 有序抖动 / 棋盘格；
  • 蓝噪声纹理（BNDS）、STBN；
  • 黄金比率 / 低差异序列（时域）。

    • 常见组合是：泊松盘定 taps 位置 + 每像素一个随机角度 θ，把整盘 taps 旋转 θ：

    所以下面讲算法时请注意它属于哪一层：泊松盘是第①层，其余全是第②层。用一张图把两层的分工固定下来：

    二、采样核层：泊松盘采样（Poisson Disk）

    2.1 为什么用它当采样核

    软阴影本质是圆盘（或球面）上的积分，tap 之间如果距离太近就是浪费——它们采到的信息高度相关。泊松盘约束任意两点最小距离 ≥ r，让有限 taps 的覆盖最均匀。下图左边是均匀网格（明显的横竖方向性 + 圆盘边缘浪费），右边是泊松盘（点距均匀、无聚集）：

    经典生成算法：

  • Dart Throwing：随机撒点，违反最小距离就丢弃，简单但慢；
  • Best-Candidate：每轮生成 k 个候选，保留离现有点集最远的那个，质量接近 dart throwing，快得多；
  • Bridson 算法（2007）：用背景网格加速，线性时间，是离线生成的常用选择。

    • 实际项目里不需要运行时生成——离线生成一次，硬编码成常量数组：

    // 16 tap 泊松盘（示意，实际数值由离线 best-candidate 生成）const vec2 poissonDisk[16] = vec2[](    vec2(-0.9420, -0.3993), vec2( 0.9455,  0.7689),    vec2(-0.0941, -0.9293), vec2( 0.3449,  0.2938),    vec2(-0.9158,  0.4577), vec2(-0.8154, -0.8791),    vec2(-0.3827,  0.2767), vec2( 0.9748,  0.7564),    vec2( 0.4432, -0.9751), vec2( 0.5374, -0.4737),    vec2(-0.2649, -0.4184), vec2( 0.7919,  0.1909),    vec2(-0.2418,  0.9970), vec2(-0.1998, -0.0733),    vec2( 0.1715, -0.4562), vec2(-0.2911,  0.6493));

    2.2 配合逐像素旋转去 banding

    float ShadowPCF(sampler2DShadow shadowMap, vec3 shadowCoord, float radius, float theta){    float s = sin(theta), c = cos(theta);    mat2 rot = mat2(c, -s, s, c);    float sum = 0.0;    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {        vec2 offset = rot * poissonDisk[i] * radius;        sum += texture(shadowMap, vec3(shadowCoord.xy + offset, shadowCoord.z));    }    return sum / 16.0;}

    θ 从哪里来？这正是第②层各算法的分工。

    三、逐像素抖动层：六种主流方案

    3.1 白噪声与哈希：最朴素的起点

    fract-sin 哈希（GPU 上最常用的伪随机）：

    float rand(vec2 p) {    return fract(sin(dot(p, vec2(12.9898, 78.233))) * 43758.5453);}float theta = rand(gl_FragCoord.xy) * 6.2831853;

    Wang Hash（整数域，质量好于 fract-sin，无精度问题）：

    uint wang_hash(uint seed){    seed = (seed ^ 61u) ^ (seed >> 16u);    seed *= 9u;    seed = seed ^ (seed >> 4u);    seed *= 0x27d4eb2du;    seed = seed ^ (seed >> 15u);    return seed;}// 用法：theta = float(wang_hash(uint(gl_FragCoord.x) * 1973u//            ^ uint(gl_FragCoord.y) * 9277u)) * (1.0/4294967296.0) * 6.2831853;

    问题：白噪声的频谱是全频段平坦的，包含大量低频能量。低频噪声 = 大块的明暗斑块，时域滤波很难收敛干净，视觉上就是「擦不掉的脏」。这正是后面所有算法要解决的问题。

    下面这张对比图是理解整篇文章的关键。上排是白噪声，右侧频谱图中心（低频区）能量很强；下排是蓝噪声，空间上看更「均匀细碎」，频谱中心是一个明显的空洞——低频能量被彻底抽走，只留高频。人眼对低频最敏感，所以蓝噪声「看起来」误差最小：

    一个常见误区：Wang Hash 只是「更好的白噪声生成器」，它并不改善噪声的频谱形状。要改善频谱，得换空间分布结构。

    3.2 Interleaved Gradient Noise（IGN）

    来自 Jorge Jimenez（Activision）的 Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty（SIGGRAPH 2014）。核心观察：有规律的、梯度交错的小结构噪声，比白噪声更容易被 TAA 吸收。

    公式极其简洁：

    float ign(vec2 pixel){    return fract(52.9829189 * fract(0.06711056 * pixel.x                                  + 0.00583715 * pixel.y));}float theta = ign(gl_FragCoord.xy) * 6.2831853;

    特点：

  • 零纹理、零状态、一个 MAD 指令级别，几乎是免费的；
  • 空间上是规则的梯度交错图案，低频能量比白噪声少；
  • 和 TAA 配合极佳（CoD 的 SSR、体积雾都靠它）；
  • 单帧静态看会有轻微规则纹理感，动起来或累积后消失。

    • 3.3 Bayer 有序抖动与棋盘格

    Bayer 矩阵是最经典的有序抖动，4x4 版本（值除以 16 归一化）：

    特点是「最大化已点亮像素之间的距离」，频谱上能量被推到高频，类似粗糙版的蓝噪声。优点是完全确定、可平铺；缺点是规则图案在静态画面上能被看出来（复古抖动风格）。

    棋盘格（checkerboard）是 2x2 Bayer 的特例，但它的用法不太一样——不是拿来生成 θ，而是拿来砍采样量：

  • 棋盘格的一种颜色采「样本集合 A」，另一种颜色采「样本集合 B」，每像素成本减半；
  • 帧奇偶时间翻转：偶数帧像素 (x+y) 为偶时采 A，奇数帧翻转采 B。两帧合起来每个像素都覆盖过 A 和 B，TAA 一累积就是全量采样：
    • bool parity = ((int(gl_FragCoord.x) + int(gl_FragCoord.y) + frameIndex) & 1) == 0;vec2 offset = rot * (parity ? tapsA[i] : tapsB[i]);

    这是「空间欠采样 + 时间补偿」的思路，在半分辨率阴影、半分辨率 AO 里非常常见。前提是你的 TAA 足够稳，否则翻转帧之间会闪。

    3.4 蓝噪声纹理（Blue Noise / BNDS）

    蓝噪声的定义是频谱上只有高频能量、低频区为空的噪声。人眼对低频敏感、对高频迟钝，所以同样的采样误差，按蓝噪声分布「看起来」最少。

    与 Bayer 的区别：Bayer 是规则周期图案，蓝噪声是无规则但满足最小距离约束的分布——可以把它理解成「抖动的泊松盘」。

  • 离线用 Void-and-Cluster（Ulichney 1993）算法生成，并做边缘回绕使其可无缝平铺；
  • 运行时一次纹理 fetch，按屏幕坐标取模寻址：
    • float theta = texelFetch(blueNoiseTex,    ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) % textureSize(blueNoiseTex, 0), 0).r * 6.2831853;
  • 工程界有现成的免费高质量蓝噪声纹理（如 Christoph Peters 的 Moments in Graphics 博客提供的 STBN/BNDS 资源），Unity HDRP、Unreal 引擎内部也都是直接内置蓝噪声纹理。

    • 定位：第②层的「单帧质量天花板」，代价是一张纹理。没有时域累积的纯前向渲染里，蓝噪声通常是最佳选择。

    3.5 时空蓝噪声（STBN）

    蓝噪声只优化了空间维。如果渲染是逐帧变化 + 时域累积的，理想情况是：每一帧在空间上是蓝噪声，同一像素在时间维也去相关。

    这里要澄清一个常见的出处混淆。业界有两条相关但不同的路线：

  • Heitz & Belcour, SIGGRAPH 2019（A Low-Discrepancy Sampler that Distributes Monte Carlo Errors as a Blue Noise in Screen Space）：思路是逐像素重排采样序列，让蒙特卡洛误差在屏幕空间上呈蓝噪声分布，本质是「样本置换 + 空间蓝噪声掩码」，并不是一张 3D 纹理。
  • Wolfe et al. (NVIDIA), EGSR 2022（Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks，即通常说的 STBN 纹理）：把蓝噪声掩码直接做成 3D 纹理，xy 是屏幕空间，z 是帧序号——下面代码里 
    stbnTex
     用的就是这套。

    • 以 3D 纹理版 STBN 为例，它的两个核心性质是：

  • 每个 z 切片单独看都是一张合法的空间蓝噪声；
  • 沿 z 轴（时间维）看，同一像素在相邻帧的取值也满足蓝噪声关系，误差互相「错开」，时域滤波收敛极快。

    • 用一张图理解这块 3D 纹理的寻址：xy 平面按屏幕坐标取模，帧号沿 z 轴推进，每帧取一个切片：

    用法和 2D 蓝噪声一样，只是寻址多一维：

    float theta = texelFetch(stbnTex,    ivec3(ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) % size, frameIndex % depth), 0).r * 6.2831853;

    定位：有时域管线的现代引擎首选，代价几乎可以忽略，收益直接反映在 TAA 收敛速度上。

    3.6 黄金比率与低差异序列（时域去相关的数学优雅版）

    不想带纹理？可以用加性递归低差异序列直接在 shader 里算时域抖动。

    一维版本就是黄金比率序列。黄金比率 phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2 ≈ 1.618 是「最无理的数」，用它做步长取小数部分，得到的序列永不重复、永不聚集：

    二维推广是 Martin Roberts 的 R2 序列（The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quasirandom Sequences）：取塑性常数 psi ≈ 1.324718（方程 x³ = x + 1 的实根），令

    一个常见且好用的组合是给 IGN 加时域动画：让 IGN 的输出随帧叠加一个黄金比 / R2 步长的偏移，使空间上的规则图案每帧平移，TAA 下迅速收敛（Jimenez 在原演讲里用的是逐帧加一个黄金比偏移，这里用 R2 常数是同一思路的二维推广）：

    float animatedIGN(vec2 pixel, int frame){    const float r2 = 0.7548776662;    frame = frame % 64;              // 防浮点精度衰减    return fract(ign(pixel) + float(frame) * r2);}

    另一类低差异序列（Halton、Sobol）更多出现在路径追踪和上采样抖动（如 TAA 的 Halton(2,3) 相机 jitter），思路相同：用数学上保证均匀且不重复的序列替代随机。

    四、横向对比

    算法作用层频谱特性时间稳定性运行时成本典型适用场景
    泊松盘采样①采样核定 taps 位置—离线预生成，免费一切软阴影/PCSS 的 taps 布局
    fract-sin / 白噪声②抖动源全频段，低频差逐帧闪烁几条 ALU快速原型、有时域累积兜底
    Wang Hash②抖动源同白噪声（质量更稳）逐帧闪烁整数 ALU需要高质量随机种子的场合
    IGN②抖动源中高频，低频较少静态稳定约 1 次 MAD无纹理预算 + 有 TAA
    Bayer / 棋盘格②抖动源/欠采样规则高频稳定（翻转依赖 TAA）免费半分辨率采样、复古风格
    蓝噪声 BNDS②抖动源纯高频，单帧最优静态稳定1 次纹理 fetch无累积前向渲染的质量天花板
    STBN②抖动源空间+时间双高频时域收敛最快1 次 3D fetch现代 TAA 管线首选
    黄金比率 / R2②时域序列时域均匀无重复累积收敛几条 ALU给 IGN 加动画、相机 jitter
    Halton / Sobol②时域序列低差异、可收敛累积收敛免费TAA jitter、蒙特卡洛积分

    五、实战选型建议

  • 先确定采样核：taps 用离线生成的泊松盘，别用均匀网格，这一步白捡质量。
  • 没有 TAA 的前向管线：上蓝噪声纹理（BNDS），单帧观感最好，一次 fetch 换「看不见条纹」。
  • 有 TAA 的现代管线：STBN 一步到位；不想带纹理就用 IGN + R2 时域动画，成本几乎为零，收敛略逊于 STBN 但完全够用。
  • 需要砍采样量：棋盘格 + 帧奇偶翻转，让 TAA 把另一半样本补回来。
  • 别忘了旋转：第②层的输出通常作为 θ 去旋转泊松盘（见 2.2 节），而不是直接当 shadow offset 用——旋转保持核内相关性、破坏像素间相关性，这是去 banding 的关键直觉。
  • 帧序号记得取模（如 % 64），否则大帧号下浮点精度会让低差异序列退化。

    • 六、参考资料

  • Jorge Jimenez, Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, SIGGRAPH 2014（IGN 出处）
  • Eric Heitz, Laurent Belcour et al., A Low-Discrepancy Sampler that Distributes Monte Carlo Errors as a Blue Noise in Screen Space, SIGGRAPH 2019（屏幕空间蓝噪声误差分布 / 样本重排）
  • Alan Wolfe et al. (NVIDIA), Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks, EGSR 2022（STBN 3D 纹理，本文 3.5 节所指）
  • Robert Ulichney, Void-and-Cluster Method for Dither Array Generation, 1993（蓝噪声生成）
  • Martin Roberts, The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quasirandom Sequences（R1/R2 序列）
  • Robert Bridson, Fast Poisson Disk Sampling in Arbitrary Dimensions, SIGGRAPH 2007 Sketches
  • Christoph Peters, Moments in Graphics 博客（免费 STBN/蓝噪声纹理资源）
item.content:encoded:
一句话：采样核形状与抖动是两个正交问题；抖动把低频条纹换成可被 TAA 抹掉的高频噪声。

要点：

  • PCSS 这类只能用 16–32 次采样逼近连续积分，所有像素共用同一组偏移会得到肉眼可见的条带（banding），因为相邻像素遮挡值完全相同
  • 正解是给每个像素不同抖动，把空间规则条纹打散成高频噪声——人眼更能容忍，且能被 TAA/时域累积/降噪器抹掉，而条纹不能
  • 先分清两个正交概念：采样核形状（所有像素共用的 tap 分布，均匀网格最差、泊松盘最好）与抖动（每像素偏移的时序/空间分布，白噪声→蓝噪声→时空蓝噪声）

为什么值得看：阴影抖动是所有实时软阴影实现都绕不开的一层，但多数团队只是随手叠个 hash。这篇把「核形状」与「抖动」分开讲并给出对比表与选型建议，属于可以直接拿去改 shader 的那类内容。

中文摘要：做软阴影（PCF/PCSS）或者任何有限次采样的效果，都会遇到采样点不够的问题：PCSS 里只能用 16–32 次采样逼近连续积分，若所有像素共用同一组采样偏移，得到的不是噪声而是肉眼可见的条带——同一光源下相邻像素算出的遮挡值完全相同。文章给出的统一解法是给每个像素施加不同抖动，把空间上规则的条带打散成高频噪声：噪声虽然难看，但高频部分人眼更能容忍，而且能被 TAA、时域累积或降噪器抹掉，条带则不能。全文先把两个容易混淆的概念分开——采样核的形状（所有像素共用的 tap 摆放，均匀网格最差、泊松盘最好）与抖动（每像素偏移的分布，白噪声到时空蓝噪声），再逐一给出原理、公式与可直接抄的代码，最后给对比表与实战选型建议。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：公众号·游戏AI编程与图形渲染（中文）

原文发布：2026-10-15

本期推送：2026-10-28

做软阴影（PCF / PCSS）或者任何有限次采样的效果时，都会遇到同一个问题：采样点不够用。

比如 PCSS 里你只能用 16~32 次采样去逼近一个连续积分，如果所有像素都用同一组采样偏移，结果不是噪声，而是一条一条肉眼可见的带状条纹（banding）——因为同一个光源下相邻像素算出来的遮挡值完全相同。

解决思路非常统一：给每个像素施加一个不同的抖动（dither），把空间上规则的 banding 打散成高频噪声。噪声虽然难看，但它有两个好处：

  • 高频噪声对人眼远比低频条纹「友好」；
  • 噪声可以被 TAA / 时域累积 / 降噪器轻松抹掉，而条纹不能。

    • 下面这张图就是全文的直觉起点——同一条连续的半影梯度，欠采样后变成刺眼的条纹，而抖动把条纹换成了人眼更能容忍、且可被时域滤波抹掉的噪声：

    这篇文章把阴影采样里常用的抖动算法系统梳理一遍，给出原理、公式和可直接抄的代码，最后给一张对比表和实战选型建议。

    先用一张流程图把整条采样链路串起来，后面每一节都对应图里的一个方块：

    一、先分清两个正交的概念

    很多人会把「泊松盘采样」和「蓝噪声抖动」混为一谈，其实它们作用在完全不同的环节。一个带抖动的阴影采样器，由两部分组成：

    ① 采样核的形状（所有像素共用）：n 个 tap 在圆盘/平面上怎么摆。

  • 均匀网格：最差，方向性明显；
  • 均匀圆盘（极坐标均匀）：一般；
  • 泊松盘（Poisson Disk）：任意两点距离有下限，覆盖均匀无聚集，是软阴影采样核的事实标准。

    • ② 逐像素的去相关源（每像素不同）：怎么让相邻像素用「同一核的不同旋转/不同排列」。

  • 哈希白噪声、Wang Hash；
  • IGN（Interleaved Gradient Noise）；
  • Bayer 有序抖动 / 棋盘格；
  • 蓝噪声纹理（BNDS）、STBN；
  • 黄金比率 / 低差异序列（时域）。

    • 常见组合是：泊松盘定 taps 位置 + 每像素一个随机角度 θ，把整盘 taps 旋转 θ：

    所以下面讲算法时请注意它属于哪一层：泊松盘是第①层，其余全是第②层。用一张图把两层的分工固定下来：

    二、采样核层：泊松盘采样（Poisson Disk）

    2.1 为什么用它当采样核

    软阴影本质是圆盘（或球面）上的积分，tap 之间如果距离太近就是浪费——它们采到的信息高度相关。泊松盘约束任意两点最小距离 ≥ r，让有限 taps 的覆盖最均匀。下图左边是均匀网格（明显的横竖方向性 + 圆盘边缘浪费），右边是泊松盘（点距均匀、无聚集）：

    经典生成算法：

  • Dart Throwing：随机撒点，违反最小距离就丢弃，简单但慢；
  • Best-Candidate：每轮生成 k 个候选，保留离现有点集最远的那个，质量接近 dart throwing，快得多；
  • Bridson 算法（2007）：用背景网格加速，线性时间，是离线生成的常用选择。

    • 实际项目里不需要运行时生成——离线生成一次，硬编码成常量数组：

    // 16 tap 泊松盘（示意，实际数值由离线 best-candidate 生成）const vec2 poissonDisk[16] = vec2[](    vec2(-0.9420, -0.3993), vec2( 0.9455,  0.7689),    vec2(-0.0941, -0.9293), vec2( 0.3449,  0.2938),    vec2(-0.9158,  0.4577), vec2(-0.8154, -0.8791),    vec2(-0.3827,  0.2767), vec2( 0.9748,  0.7564),    vec2( 0.4432, -0.9751), vec2( 0.5374, -0.4737),    vec2(-0.2649, -0.4184), vec2( 0.7919,  0.1909),    vec2(-0.2418,  0.9970), vec2(-0.1998, -0.0733),    vec2( 0.1715, -0.4562), vec2(-0.2911,  0.6493));

    2.2 配合逐像素旋转去 banding

    float ShadowPCF(sampler2DShadow shadowMap, vec3 shadowCoord, float radius, float theta){    float s = sin(theta), c = cos(theta);    mat2 rot = mat2(c, -s, s, c);    float sum = 0.0;    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {        vec2 offset = rot * poissonDisk[i] * radius;        sum += texture(shadowMap, vec3(shadowCoord.xy + offset, shadowCoord.z));    }    return sum / 16.0;}

    θ 从哪里来？这正是第②层各算法的分工。

    三、逐像素抖动层：六种主流方案

    3.1 白噪声与哈希：最朴素的起点

    fract-sin 哈希（GPU 上最常用的伪随机）：

    float rand(vec2 p) {    return fract(sin(dot(p, vec2(12.9898, 78.233))) * 43758.5453);}float theta = rand(gl_FragCoord.xy) * 6.2831853;

    Wang Hash（整数域，质量好于 fract-sin，无精度问题）：

    uint wang_hash(uint seed){    seed = (seed ^ 61u) ^ (seed >> 16u);    seed *= 9u;    seed = seed ^ (seed >> 4u);    seed *= 0x27d4eb2du;    seed = seed ^ (seed >> 15u);    return seed;}// 用法：theta = float(wang_hash(uint(gl_FragCoord.x) * 1973u//            ^ uint(gl_FragCoord.y) * 9277u)) * (1.0/4294967296.0) * 6.2831853;

    问题：白噪声的频谱是全频段平坦的，包含大量低频能量。低频噪声 = 大块的明暗斑块，时域滤波很难收敛干净，视觉上就是「擦不掉的脏」。这正是后面所有算法要解决的问题。

    下面这张对比图是理解整篇文章的关键。上排是白噪声，右侧频谱图中心（低频区）能量很强；下排是蓝噪声，空间上看更「均匀细碎」，频谱中心是一个明显的空洞——低频能量被彻底抽走，只留高频。人眼对低频最敏感，所以蓝噪声「看起来」误差最小：

    一个常见误区：Wang Hash 只是「更好的白噪声生成器」，它并不改善噪声的频谱形状。要改善频谱，得换空间分布结构。

    3.2 Interleaved Gradient Noise（IGN）

    来自 Jorge Jimenez（Activision）的 Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty（SIGGRAPH 2014）。核心观察：有规律的、梯度交错的小结构噪声，比白噪声更容易被 TAA 吸收。

    公式极其简洁：

    float ign(vec2 pixel){    return fract(52.9829189 * fract(0.06711056 * pixel.x                                  + 0.00583715 * pixel.y));}float theta = ign(gl_FragCoord.xy) * 6.2831853;

    特点：

  • 零纹理、零状态、一个 MAD 指令级别，几乎是免费的；
  • 空间上是规则的梯度交错图案，低频能量比白噪声少；
  • 和 TAA 配合极佳（CoD 的 SSR、体积雾都靠它）；
  • 单帧静态看会有轻微规则纹理感，动起来或累积后消失。

    • 3.3 Bayer 有序抖动与棋盘格

    Bayer 矩阵是最经典的有序抖动，4x4 版本（值除以 16 归一化）：

    特点是「最大化已点亮像素之间的距离」，频谱上能量被推到高频，类似粗糙版的蓝噪声。优点是完全确定、可平铺；缺点是规则图案在静态画面上能被看出来（复古抖动风格）。

    棋盘格（checkerboard）是 2x2 Bayer 的特例，但它的用法不太一样——不是拿来生成 θ，而是拿来砍采样量：

  • 棋盘格的一种颜色采「样本集合 A」，另一种颜色采「样本集合 B」，每像素成本减半；
  • 帧奇偶时间翻转：偶数帧像素 (x+y) 为偶时采 A，奇数帧翻转采 B。两帧合起来每个像素都覆盖过 A 和 B，TAA 一累积就是全量采样：
    • bool parity = ((int(gl_FragCoord.x) + int(gl_FragCoord.y) + frameIndex) & 1) == 0;vec2 offset = rot * (parity ? tapsA[i] : tapsB[i]);

    这是「空间欠采样 + 时间补偿」的思路，在半分辨率阴影、半分辨率 AO 里非常常见。前提是你的 TAA 足够稳，否则翻转帧之间会闪。

    3.4 蓝噪声纹理（Blue Noise / BNDS）

    蓝噪声的定义是频谱上只有高频能量、低频区为空的噪声。人眼对低频敏感、对高频迟钝，所以同样的采样误差，按蓝噪声分布「看起来」最少。

    与 Bayer 的区别：Bayer 是规则周期图案，蓝噪声是无规则但满足最小距离约束的分布——可以把它理解成「抖动的泊松盘」。

  • 离线用 Void-and-Cluster（Ulichney 1993）算法生成，并做边缘回绕使其可无缝平铺；
  • 运行时一次纹理 fetch，按屏幕坐标取模寻址：
    • float theta = texelFetch(blueNoiseTex,    ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) % textureSize(blueNoiseTex, 0), 0).r * 6.2831853;
  • 工程界有现成的免费高质量蓝噪声纹理（如 Christoph Peters 的 Moments in Graphics 博客提供的 STBN/BNDS 资源），Unity HDRP、Unreal 引擎内部也都是直接内置蓝噪声纹理。

    • 定位：第②层的「单帧质量天花板」，代价是一张纹理。没有时域累积的纯前向渲染里，蓝噪声通常是最佳选择。

    3.5 时空蓝噪声（STBN）

    蓝噪声只优化了空间维。如果渲染是逐帧变化 + 时域累积的，理想情况是：每一帧在空间上是蓝噪声，同一像素在时间维也去相关。

    这里要澄清一个常见的出处混淆。业界有两条相关但不同的路线：

  • Heitz & Belcour, SIGGRAPH 2019（A Low-Discrepancy Sampler that Distributes Monte Carlo Errors as a Blue Noise in Screen Space）：思路是逐像素重排采样序列，让蒙特卡洛误差在屏幕空间上呈蓝噪声分布，本质是「样本置换 + 空间蓝噪声掩码」，并不是一张 3D 纹理。
  • Wolfe et al. (NVIDIA), EGSR 2022（Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks，即通常说的 STBN 纹理）：把蓝噪声掩码直接做成 3D 纹理，xy 是屏幕空间，z 是帧序号——下面代码里 
    stbnTex
     用的就是这套。

    • 以 3D 纹理版 STBN 为例，它的两个核心性质是：

  • 每个 z 切片单独看都是一张合法的空间蓝噪声；
  • 沿 z 轴（时间维）看，同一像素在相邻帧的取值也满足蓝噪声关系，误差互相「错开」，时域滤波收敛极快。

    • 用一张图理解这块 3D 纹理的寻址：xy 平面按屏幕坐标取模，帧号沿 z 轴推进，每帧取一个切片：

    用法和 2D 蓝噪声一样，只是寻址多一维：

    float theta = texelFetch(stbnTex,    ivec3(ivec2(gl_FragCoord.xy) % size, frameIndex % depth), 0).r * 6.2831853;

    定位：有时域管线的现代引擎首选，代价几乎可以忽略，收益直接反映在 TAA 收敛速度上。

    3.6 黄金比率与低差异序列（时域去相关的数学优雅版）

    不想带纹理？可以用加性递归低差异序列直接在 shader 里算时域抖动。

    一维版本就是黄金比率序列。黄金比率 phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2 ≈ 1.618 是「最无理的数」，用它做步长取小数部分，得到的序列永不重复、永不聚集：

    二维推广是 Martin Roberts 的 R2 序列（The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quasirandom Sequences）：取塑性常数 psi ≈ 1.324718（方程 x³ = x + 1 的实根），令

    一个常见且好用的组合是给 IGN 加时域动画：让 IGN 的输出随帧叠加一个黄金比 / R2 步长的偏移，使空间上的规则图案每帧平移，TAA 下迅速收敛（Jimenez 在原演讲里用的是逐帧加一个黄金比偏移，这里用 R2 常数是同一思路的二维推广）：

    float animatedIGN(vec2 pixel, int frame){    const float r2 = 0.7548776662;    frame = frame % 64;              // 防浮点精度衰减    return fract(ign(pixel) + float(frame) * r2);}

    另一类低差异序列（Halton、Sobol）更多出现在路径追踪和上采样抖动（如 TAA 的 Halton(2,3) 相机 jitter），思路相同：用数学上保证均匀且不重复的序列替代随机。

    四、横向对比

    算法作用层频谱特性时间稳定性运行时成本典型适用场景
    泊松盘采样①采样核定 taps 位置—离线预生成，免费一切软阴影/PCSS 的 taps 布局
    fract-sin / 白噪声②抖动源全频段，低频差逐帧闪烁几条 ALU快速原型、有时域累积兜底
    Wang Hash②抖动源同白噪声（质量更稳）逐帧闪烁整数 ALU需要高质量随机种子的场合
    IGN②抖动源中高频，低频较少静态稳定约 1 次 MAD无纹理预算 + 有 TAA
    Bayer / 棋盘格②抖动源/欠采样规则高频稳定（翻转依赖 TAA）免费半分辨率采样、复古风格
    蓝噪声 BNDS②抖动源纯高频，单帧最优静态稳定1 次纹理 fetch无累积前向渲染的质量天花板
    STBN②抖动源空间+时间双高频时域收敛最快1 次 3D fetch现代 TAA 管线首选
    黄金比率 / R2②时域序列时域均匀无重复累积收敛几条 ALU给 IGN 加动画、相机 jitter
    Halton / Sobol②时域序列低差异、可收敛累积收敛免费TAA jitter、蒙特卡洛积分

    五、实战选型建议

  • 先确定采样核：taps 用离线生成的泊松盘，别用均匀网格，这一步白捡质量。
  • 没有 TAA 的前向管线：上蓝噪声纹理（BNDS），单帧观感最好，一次 fetch 换「看不见条纹」。
  • 有 TAA 的现代管线：STBN 一步到位；不想带纹理就用 IGN + R2 时域动画，成本几乎为零，收敛略逊于 STBN 但完全够用。
  • 需要砍采样量：棋盘格 + 帧奇偶翻转，让 TAA 把另一半样本补回来。
  • 别忘了旋转：第②层的输出通常作为 θ 去旋转泊松盘（见 2.2 节），而不是直接当 shadow offset 用——旋转保持核内相关性、破坏像素间相关性，这是去 banding 的关键直觉。
  • 帧序号记得取模（如 % 64），否则大帧号下浮点精度会让低差异序列退化。

    • 六、参考资料

  • Jorge Jimenez, Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, SIGGRAPH 2014（IGN 出处）
  • Eric Heitz, Laurent Belcour et al., A Low-Discrepancy Sampler that Distributes Monte Carlo Errors as a Blue Noise in Screen Space, SIGGRAPH 2019（屏幕空间蓝噪声误差分布 / 样本重排）
  • Alan Wolfe et al. (NVIDIA), Spatiotemporal Blue Noise Masks, EGSR 2022（STBN 3D 纹理，本文 3.5 节所指）
  • Robert Ulichney, Void-and-Cluster Method for Dither Array Generation, 1993（蓝噪声生成）
  • Martin Roberts, The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quasirandom Sequences（R1/R2 序列）
  • Robert Bridson, Fast Poisson Disk Sampling in Arbitrary Dimensions, SIGGRAPH 2007 Sketches
  • Christoph Peters, Moments in Graphics 博客（免费 STBN/蓝噪声纹理资源）

item.title: Godot 4.8 beta 1：功能冻结，剩下只修回归 ｜ Dev snapshot: Godot 4.8 beta 1
item.description:
一句话：4.8 进入 feature freeze，开发资源全部转向回归修复与 bug 狩猎冲刺。

要点：

  • Beta 1 意味着 4.8 已完整进入 feature freeze：新特性不再合入，开发资源全部转向创建与评审回归修复
  • 官方邀请社区参加 bug-hunting sprint（需先读 Bug Triage Introduction，并加入 #bugsquad 频道）
  • 对使用方来说，这是评估升级窗口的信号：从现在到 rc 之间接口基本稳定，适合开始跑自家项目的回归

为什么值得看：引擎版本节点的价值在于「什么时候可以安全升级」。beta 1 的 feature freeze 就是那个时间点：想跟 4.8 的团队现在就该把项目拉上去跑回归，而不是等到正式版才发现问题。

中文摘要：Godot 4.8 发布 beta 1 快照，意味着这个版本已完整进入 feature freeze：不再合入新特性，开发资源全部转向创建与评审各类回归修复。官方同时邀请社区参加 bug-hunting sprint——参与者需先阅读 Bug Triage Introduction，并加入 #bugsquad 与 #bugsquad-sprints 频道。对使用 Godot 的团队来说，这条短消息的实际意义是给出了升级窗口：从现在到 rc 之间对外接口基本稳定，适合把自家项目拉起来跑一轮回归，把问题尽量暴露在正式版之前，而不是等到发版才发现。

主题：游戏引擎

来源：Godot（English）

原文发布：2026-10-15

本期推送：2026-10-28

Dev snapshot: Godot 4.8 beta 1

By: Thaddeus Crews15 October 2026Pre-release

It’s that time of the release cycle once again: the beta snapshot! With this, 4.8 is fully in feature-freeze, and developer resources have shifted exclusively to creating and reviewing various regression fixes.

For those interested in aiding us on our quest to squash any bugs that come up during this time, we once again encourage you to join our bug-hunting sprints. Anyone interested should read the Bug Triage Introduction for more information, and join the 

#bugsquad
and 
#bugsquad-sprints
 channels on our developer RocketChat to participate.

Please consider supporting the project financially, if you are able. Godot is maintained by the efforts of volunteers and a small team of paid contributors. Your donations go towards sponsoring their work and ensuring they can dedicate their undivided attention to the needs of the project.

Jump to the Downloads section, and give it a spin right now, or continue reading to learn more about improvements in this release. You can also try the Web editor, the XR editor, or the Android editor for this release. If you are interested in the latter, please request to join our testing group to get access to pre-release builds.

The cover illustration is fromRita, a puzzle game with platforming elements, featuring a wide variety of word puzzles within a cozy world. You can buy the game on Steam, and follow the developer on Bluesky, YouTube, and itch.io.

Highlights

For those who have been following our development snapshots closely, you may be familiar with a number of the highlights in this post which were already covered in previous articles (4.8 dev 1, 4.8 dev 2, 4.8 dev 3, 4.8 dev 4, 4.8 dev 5, 4.8 dev 6, and 4.8 dev 7).

Because we’re already in feature freeze, there are no new features to cover compared to dev 7. Instead, we’ll focus on a general round-up of what to expect from Godot 4.8 as a whole, as well as expanding on some additions that we didn’t have the chance to highlight in our previous snapshots.

  • Breaking changes
  • 3D
  • Core
  • Documentation
  • Editor
  • GDScript
  • GUI
  • Input
  • Physics
  • Platforms
  • Rendering and shaders
  • Shaders
  • XR

    • Breaking changes

    We try to minimize breaking changes, but sometimes they are necessary in order to fix high-priority issues. Where we do break compatibility, we do our best to make sure that the changes are minimal and require few changes in user projects.

    You can find a list of such issues by filtering the merged PRs in the 4.8 milestone with the 

    breaks compat
    label.

  • 3D: Remove undocumented script only enter_world callbacks (GH-111504).
  • Animation: Fix 
    LookAtModifier3D.is_interpolating()
    value is inverted (GH-121391).
  • Animation: Make Bone Follower classes’ FTI off as default, add warning (GH-119509).
  • Core: Fail when trying to use local debugger in release exports (GH-122213).
  • Editor: Fix corner cases related to scroll hints across the editor (GH-117080).
  • Editor: Remove 
    ScriptServer
    fallbacks from 
    ClassDB
    (GH-123379).
  • Export: Do not serialize export options that do not have the 
    PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE
    flag (GH-120721).
  • GDScript: Forbid scripts from inheriting their own inner classes (GH-121171).
  • GUI: Fix duplicated button press event on touch input (GH-120864).
  • GUI: Rework dialog default titles (GH-105550).
  • Input: Ignore joypads on unfocused window by default for new projects (GH-120399).
  • Network: mbedTLS: Update to 4.1.0, PSA Crypto (GH-120725).
  • Platforms: Android: Make 
    OS.alert()
    blocking (GH-120800).
  • Rendering: Add support for ASTC 6x6 and high quality compression profiles (GH-115003).
  • Rendering: Fix sky shader 
    SCREEN_UV
    builtin in Compatibility renderer (GH-121676).
  • XR: OpenXR use proper spatial entity NULL constant (GH-121815).

    • 3D

    QbieShay starts our feature round-up strong with 

    Trail3D
    . Introduced in GH-117107 and built off the foundation by Zi Ye’s Cozy Cube Godot Addons, this native solution enables those seeking stunning visual effects through trails to no longer require deep knowledge of how meshes are drawn, UVs are assigned, or anything of the sort; everything Just Works™.

    While being more of an editor feature, the 3D Viewport override functionality by Michael Alexsander in GH-117569 warrants a highlight in this section. Through the new editor option “Allow Viewport Override” (enabled by default), hovering the mouse over a viewport set to a specific side will cause the currently edited axis to match that side.

    And more:

  • Add octant visualization to 
    GridMap
    (GH-118583).
  • 3D: Re-enable freelook inertia by default in the 3D editor (GH-121478).

    • Core

    Adam Johnston brought us “Fuzzy searching” with GH-98278, enabling search results to return matches similar to the passed query, rather than only returning an exact match. Now with GH-107126, this functionality is finally ready to roll for all users.

    var items := ["Potion of Healing", "Greater Health Potion", "Poison Vial"]
var fuzzy := FuzzySearch.new()

for result in fuzzy.search_all("health potion", items):
	# Prints "Greater Health Potion", "Potion of Healing".
	print(result.target)

    Those using version control will be thrilled to hear that serialization of objects has become much cleaner starting with GH-92102. Robert Wallis ensures that all objects are now formatted such that they won’t cause oversized diffs.

    BeforeAfter

    And more:

  • Core: Add support for metadata in text scenes (GH-121920).
  • Core: Introduce 
    Variant.to()
    as a replacement to implicit conversions from 
    Variant
    (GH-123600).
  • Core: Make it impossible to have more than one main thread, and don’t release unnecessarily (GH-121161).
  • Core: Move property maps from 
    ClassDB
    to 
    GDType
    . Accelerate 
    Object
    property access 1.6x (GH-122596).
  • Core: Simplify 
    GDType
    by storing all properties in a single unified map. Save ~12mb runtime RAM (GH-122751).
  • Core: Speed up removing many child nodes (GH-120942).

    • Documentation

    Cyril Bissey’s efforts in GH-111375 grants our documentation—both in-editor and online—native support for admonitions; That being: the built-in systems many documentation tools provide to highlight crucial information. As time of writing, our documentation tools use simple prefixes like “Note:” or “Warning:” to convey a similar effect, but this method causes critical details to blend in with the rest of the text. So starting now, we’ll begin slowly rolling out admonition replacements for these legacy systems, which will end up looking something like what you see below:

    Dark ModeLight Mode

    Editor

    Ever since the introduction of the 

    EditorDock
    in Godot 4.6, Tomasz Chabora has been on a journey to migrate our existing editor plugins to this new system. The most ambitious migration yet occurred with GH-113051, which converts the main screen itself into a dock. This is a very fundamental change to how the editor is handled, but the benefits that are immediately available are more than worth it.

    As a result of these changes:

  • The main screen editors aren’t tied to specific plugins anymore, instead being regular 
    EditorDock
    s.
  • Main screen docks have their own editor setting for tab style.
  • All main screens can be closed.
  • All main screens can float.
  • The only exception is Game, as custom behavior is currently tightly integrated with 
    WindowWrapper
    .

    • Complimenting the new structure of our editor are new and improved toolbars for our various main screens. Jayden Sipe delivered three fantastic overhauls to the Game, 2D, and 3D panels with GH-118664, GH-121080, and GH-121065 respectively. All three being spearheaded by the same creative vision ensures a uniform style; one which heavily emphasizes usability and clarity in comparison to the prior implementations.

    BeforeAfter
    Game
    2D
    3D

    Mikael Hermansson delivers the ability to drag-toggle visibility in the scene tree editor with GH-118634. Now when toggling the visibility of a given node, the newly toggled state can be applied to any subsequent nodes when dragging the mouse across them.

    It’s never been easier to make a title more accessible to users across multiple languages, thanks to the use of pseudolocalization. Tomasz Chabora, seeking to further expand the utility and awareness of our language hot-swap functionality, enabled pseudolocalization within the editor itself in GH-119443. This simple toggle simulates changes that might take place during localization, allowing any issues that would come from that process to be recognized as early as possible in development.

    Hugo Locurcio’s work in GH-99725 brought a long-desired QOL addition to the inspector: auto-expansion of resources. While most of our inspector items automatically revealed themselves when initialized, resources always existed as an unfortunate blindspot. As demonstrated below, this will no longer be the case!

    DexterFstone made it possible to play a scene from the file system directly in GH-111941. Now any scene can be played from the file system’s context menu alone; no extra steps required!

    Jayden returns with two more editor goodies in GH-119103, aiming to expand the QOL for our 

    FileSystem
    logic. The first of these features is the ability to zoom in/out of the window with a mouse’s scrollwheel. By simply holding 
    Ctrl
    while hovering over a 
    FileSystem
    window, the contents will either grow or shrink upon scrolling the mouse up or down respectively.

    Next up is glob-based searching. Sometimes you want to find a type of file or something with a specific prefix, without necessarily narrowing it down to a specific file. By utilizing glob-based search, now your results can explicitly capture whatever use-case you desire.

    Michael Alexsander keeps the editor train rolling with another highly-requested feature: runtime manipulation of 

    CanvasItem
    s! Thanks to his work in GH-122510, the following functionality is now fully integrated within Godot 4.8 (lifted verbatim from the original PR):

  • Movement, resizing, rotation, scaling, and pivot modification of 
    CanvasItem
    s, together with its own toolbar.
  • Full undo/redo support, unified in the editor’s undo/redo manager.
  • Added the ability to open scenes by double-clicking them in the game. Just like how it’s done in the editor.
  • Improved remote shortcut handling. Which is now funneled into a single debugger message, and triggers the pressed visual on the buttons.
  • Improved mouse cursor updates in the editor. Now they trigger immediately rather than after an action is taken with the mouse again.

    • We’ll end our editor highlights with symbol renaming, an experimental feature brought to us by Tomasz with GH-117949. With this, renaming a symbol will properly propogate that logic across the project, uniformly applying the rename where relevant.

    And more:

  • Add an option to run the project upgrade tool when updating to a new Godot version (GH-119466).
  • Add Clear Project Cache option (GH-120093).
  • Add replace preview to Find in Files (GH-122659).
  • Add toggle button for texture preview metadata overlay (GH-117216).
  • Automatically create default resources in the editor for many objects (GH-88647).
  • Clean and simplify 
    Inspector
    header (GH-117499).
  • Embed the game view in the main editor window as the default (GH-120736).
  • Fix metadata formatting in inspector (GH-108878).
  • List monitor resolutions and refresh rates in editor Copy System Info (GH-122809).
  • Make main screen dock colors more readable (GH-122903).
  • Show doc tooltips in quick settings (GH-121278).
  • Show enum integer values in inspector tooltips (GH-102734).
  • Show inspector warning on deprecated properties (GH-121364).
  • Turn the script method outline into a 
    Tree
    (GH-121534).
  • Use VHS Circle as the default editor color picker shape (GH-110615).

    • GDScript

    Courtesy of Malcolm Anderson in GH-119588, the debugging process for GDScript will become much more streamlined thanks to the direct and immediate information provided by underlined warnings. While you would previously have a line with a warning/error be highlighted if a problem existed, it highlighted the entire line, which both obfuscated the problem and risked multiple issues being hidden if they existed on the same line. With these changes, only the relevant portions of a given line will be underlined. For instance, the following codeblock would’ve previously been highlighted in its entirety:

    And more:

  • Disallow strings as comments (GH-121833).
  • Fix shutdown crash when 
    ScriptInstance
    references its owner (GH-121762).
  • Improve performance for Syntax Highlighting (GH-123320).
  • Make language shutdown more crash resilient (GH-120976).

    • GUI

    Every developer knows the struggle of text container constraints all too well. No matter how reasonable you think your font scale is, or what kind of variable text you believe can make it in, a translation string or player input will inevitably break those bounds. Even if you actively and thoroughly filter all input length at all times, that’s still a lot of code upkeep and boilerplating across different areas of your project to achieve the desired effect.

    Ismail Ivanov is one of many who felt this struggle of our text container constraints, and decided to do something about it. GH-116791 grants 

    Label
    and 
    RichTextLabel
    resize-to-fit functionality, utilizing three newly-added properties: 
    auto_font_size
    , 
    min_font_size
    , and 
    max_font_size
    .

    One of the most common requests we’ve seen for improving 

    Tree
    functionality is the ability to support “sticky items”. That is: the ability for a given line to stick to the top if it represents a foldable region. Koliur Rahman is no stranger to integrating popular editor requests, so it was only a matter of time before they delivered the desired functionality in GH-115697.

    And more:

  • Add 
    format
    property to SpinBox and deprecate 
    prefix
    /
    suffix
    (GH-103998).
  • Add new default algorithm of automatic focus strategy for 
    Control
    nodes (GH-120631).
  • Audio: Add theme sound items and playback on common UI events (GH-111455).
  • TabBar: Add options for tab sizing strategy (GH-113385).
  • Use OS taskbar progress when 
    ProgressDialog
    is shown (GH-121505).

    • Input

    Many of our existing GUI items have received native touch support in 4.8, warranting a separate input-focused section dedicated to showcasing their new functionality. All of the following featured items come courtesy of Anish Kumar.

    Starting with GH-119706’s two-for-one package deal, both 

    TextEdit
    and 
    CodeEdit

Introduced in GH-117107 and built off the foundation by Zi Ye’s Cozy Cube Godot Addons, this native solution enables those seeking stunning visual effects through trails to no longer require deep knowledge of how meshes are drawn, UVs are assigned, or anything of the sort; everything Just Works™.

    While being more of an editor feature, the 3D Viewport override functionality by Michael Alexsander in GH-117569 warrants a highlight in this section. Through the new editor option “Allow Viewport Override” (enabled by default), hovering the mouse over a viewport set to a specific side will cause the currently edited axis to match that side.

    And more:

  • Add octant visualization to 
    GridMap
    (GH-118583).
  • 3D: Re-enable freelook inertia by default in the 3D editor (GH-121478).

    • Core

    Adam Johnston brought us “Fuzzy searching” with GH-98278, enabling search results to return matches similar to the passed query, rather than only returning an exact match. Now with GH-107126, this functionality is finally ready to roll for all users.

    var items := ["Potion of Healing", "Greater Health Potion", "Poison Vial"]
var fuzzy := FuzzySearch.new()

for result in fuzzy.search_all("health potion", items):
	# Prints "Greater Health Potion", "Potion of Healing".
	print(result.target)

    Those using version control will be thrilled to hear that serialization of objects has become much cleaner starting with GH-92102. Robert Wallis ensures that all objects are now formatted such that they won’t cause oversized diffs.

    BeforeAfter

    And more:

  • Core: Add support for metadata in text scenes (GH-121920).
  • Core: Introduce 
    Variant.to()
    as a replacement to implicit conversions from 
    Variant
    (GH-123600).
  • Core: Make it impossible to have more than one main thread, and don’t release unnecessarily (GH-121161).
  • Core: Move property maps from 
    ClassDB
    to 
    GDType
    . Accelerate 
    Object
    property access 1.6x (GH-122596).
  • Core: Simplify 
    GDType
    by storing all properties in a single unified map. Save ~12mb runtime RAM (GH-122751).
  • Core: Speed up removing many child nodes (GH-120942).

    • Documentation

    Cyril Bissey’s efforts in GH-111375 grants our documentation—both in-editor and online—native support for admonitions; That being: the built-in systems many documentation tools provide to highlight crucial information. As time of writing, our documentation tools use simple prefixes like “Note:” or “Warning:” to convey a similar effect, but this method causes critical details to blend in with the rest of the text. So starting now, we’ll begin slowly rolling out admonition replacements for these legacy systems, which will end up looking something like what you see below:

    Dark ModeLight Mode

    Editor

    Ever since the introduction of the 

    EditorDock
    in Godot 4.6, Tomasz Chabora has been on a journey to migrate our existing editor plugins to this new system. The most ambitious migration yet occurred with GH-113051, which converts the main screen itself into a dock. This is a very fundamental change to how the editor is handled, but the benefits that are immediately available are more than worth it.

    As a result of these changes:

  • The main screen editors aren’t tied to specific plugins anymore, instead being regular 
    EditorDock
    s.
  • Main screen docks have their own editor setting for tab style.
  • All main screens can be closed.
  • All main screens can float.
  • The only exception is Game, as custom behavior is currently tightly integrated with 
    WindowWrapper
    .

    • Complimenting the new structure of our editor are new and improved toolbars for our various main screens. Jayden Sipe delivered three fantastic overhauls to the Game, 2D, and 3D panels with GH-118664, GH-121080, and GH-121065 respectively. All three being spearheaded by the same creative vision ensures a uniform style; one which heavily emphasizes usability and clarity in comparison to the prior implementations.

    BeforeAfter
    Game
    2D
    3D

    Mikael Hermansson delivers the ability to drag-toggle visibility in the scene tree editor with GH-118634. Now when toggling the visibility of a given node, the newly toggled state can be applied to any subsequent nodes when dragging the mouse across them.

    It’s never been easier to make a title more accessible to users across multiple languages, thanks to the use of pseudolocalization. Tomasz Chabora, seeking to further expand the utility and awareness of our language hot-swap functionality, enabled pseudolocalization within the editor itself in GH-119443. This simple toggle simulates changes that might take place during localization, allowing any issues that would come from that process to be recognized as early as possible in development.

    Hugo Locurcio’s work in GH-99725 brought a long-desired QOL addition to the inspector: auto-expansion of resources. While most of our inspector items automatically revealed themselves when initialized, resources always existed as an unfortunate blindspot. As demonstrated below, this will no longer be the case!

    DexterFstone made it possible to play a scene from the file system directly in GH-111941. Now any scene can be played from the file system’s context menu alone; no extra steps required!

    Jayden returns with two more editor goodies in GH-119103, aiming to expand the QOL for our 

    FileSystem
    logic. The first of these features is the ability to zoom in/out of the window with a mouse’s scrollwheel. By simply holding 
    Ctrl
    while hovering over a 
    FileSystem
    window, the contents will either grow or shrink upon scrolling the mouse up or down respectively.

    Next up is glob-based searching. Sometimes you want to find a type of file or something with a specific prefix, without necessarily narrowing it down to a specific file. By utilizing glob-based search, now your results can explicitly capture whatever use-case you desire.

    Michael Alexsander keeps the editor train rolling with another highly-requested feature: runtime manipulation of 

    CanvasItem
    s! Thanks to his work in GH-122510, the following functionality is now fully integrated within Godot 4.8 (lifted verbatim from the original PR):

  • Movement, resizing, rotation, scaling, and pivot modification of 
    CanvasItem
    s, together with its own toolbar.
  • Full undo/redo support, unified in the editor’s undo/redo manager.
  • Added the ability to open scenes by double-clicking them in the game. Just like how it’s done in the editor.
  • Improved remote shortcut handling. Which is now funneled into a single debugger message, and triggers the pressed visual on the buttons.
  • Improved mouse cursor updates in the editor. Now they trigger immediately rather than after an action is taken with the mouse again.

    • We’ll end our editor highlights with symbol renaming, an experimental feature brought to us by Tomasz with GH-117949. With this, renaming a symbol will properly propogate that logic across the project, uniformly applying the rename where relevant.

    And more:

  • Add replace preview to Find in Files (GH-122659).

    Inspector
    header (GH-117499).

  • Show doc tooltips in quick settings (GH-121278).
  • Show enum integer values in inspector tooltips (GH-102734).
  • Show inspector warning on deprecated properties (GH-121364).
  • Turn the script method outline into a 
    Tree
    (GH-121534).
  • Use VHS Circle as the default editor color picker shape (GH-110615).

    • GDScript

    Courtesy of Malcolm Anderson in GH-119588, the debugging process for GDScript will become much more streamlined thanks to the direct and immediate information provided by underlined warnings. While you would previously have a line with a warning/error be highlighted if a problem existed, it highlighted the entire line, which both obfuscated the problem and risked multiple issues being hidden if they existed on the same line. With these changes, only the relevant portions of a given line will be underlined. For instance, the following codeblock would’ve previously been highlighted in its entirety:

  • Fix shutdown crash when 
    ScriptInstance
    references its owner (GH-121762).
  • Improve performance for Syntax Highlighting (GH-123320).
  • Make language shutdown more crash resilient (GH-120976).

    • GUI

    Every developer knows the struggle of text container constraints all too well. No matter how reasonable you think your font scale is, or what kind of variable text you believe can make it in, a translation string or player input will inevitably break those bounds. Even if you actively and thoroughly filter all input length at all times, that’s still a lot of code upkeep and boilerplating across different areas of your project to achieve the desired effect.

    Ismail Ivanov is one of many who felt this struggle of our text container constraints, and decided to do something about it. GH-116791 grants 

    Label
    and

    resize-to-fit functionality, utilizing three newly-added properties:

    ,

    , and

    .

    One of the most common requests we’ve seen for improving 

    Tree
    functionality is the ability to support “sticky items”. That is: the ability for a given line to stick to the top if it represents a foldable region. Koliur Rahman is no stranger to integrating popular editor requests, so it was only a matter of time before they delivered the desired functionality in GH-115697.

    And more:

    prefix
    /

    (GH-103998).

    Control
    nodes (GH-120631).
  • Audio: Add theme sound items and playback on common UI events (GH-111455).
  • TabBar: Add options for tab sizing strategy (GH-113385).
  • Use OS taskbar progress when 
    ProgressDialog
    is shown (GH-121505).

    Many of our existing GUI items have received native touch support in 4.8, warranting a separate input-focused section dedicated to showcasing their new functionality. All of the following featured items come courtesy of Anish Kumar.

    Starting with GH-119706’s two-for-one package deal, both 

    TextEdit
    and
